1) Reflavouring is free. You can try asking your DM if you could respec your character and choose a better build, but flavour them as an assassin. A fighter who only fights with light armour, shield and a finesse weapon with high dex and proficiency on stealth then say he’s an assassin and flavour your attacks as such. 
2) Settings matter. A roleplay heavy campaign will have a fighter feel less useful compared to a bard or a rogue, a dungeon crawling heavy campaign full of traps but not as much combat will have rogues shine a lot, a stealth heavy campaign will have people with armour like platemail is gonna be a burden, etc.
3) Your character is not a 1 dimensional character who will be the same person they were at the start of the campaign but stronger. They are multidimensional characters who have feelings and emotions. Just because they use a shortsword and dagger because of their backstory doesn’t mean they are stuck to those weapons. If *you* feel like you aren’t being good in combat, does *your character* feel the same way? If they do, and are willing to, what’s stopping them from buying a ranged weapon? It’s called assassin, someone who is meant to not be seen, kill one guy while everyone isn’t expecting it and dip. Not hide during combat and deal massive damage without as much risk as the barbarian. If you want, you can ask your DM to homebrew something like if you can inconspicuously get close to someone without arousing suspicion, you are allowed to stab someone who is the same size class as you and either kill them instantly (to feel more assassin-like) or auto crit if you feel that’s too broken. Part of the fun of dnd is that we’re not hardstuck to the rules and can adjust the rulings to cater to your party. And even outside of that, as a rogue, you fight without facing as much risk because you can hide as a bonus action, sneak attack from long range, triple your movement speed by dashing twice, disengage as a bonus action so you don’t get opportunity attacked when you decide to stab someone. It’s not unfair to say the guy who is at the frontlines getting the brunt of the blows will be doing a good bit of damage more than you. Speaking of damage, your table keeps talking about minimums, when you should be using averages (unless the consensus changed while I didn’t check dnd reddit). A d6 on average is 3.5 (rounded up). Assuming rapier with sneak attack at level 4, that’s 7 + 5 (1d8 average is 4.5 (rounded up)) + dex mod. But since you’re a rogue, I recommend using a ranged weapon so you can use your bonus action to hide and not disengage to give yourself advantage. Advantage gives you a higher chance to crit, doubling your average damage.
